messages.subject:
Re: [DISCUSS] Opt-in re-firing of asset partitions on late/corrected
 data
messages.body:
Hi Ramzi, all,
+1 on this feature. I am evaluating adopting airflow and intend to run partitioned-asset Dags for use cases where restated data for already-processed partitions is routine.
The proposed modes and opt-in seem right to me. I have no strong feelings on the implicit default when a user opts-in. This is my first interaction with the project but as there is no activity on this thread perhaps opening a PR would get traction? This feature may be light enough to not require one.
Some thoughts on implementation:

  1.  Concurrency. I had planned to propose this already but a per-partition-key active-run limit, like the Dag-wide max_active_runs, would be useful, e.g. with NewRun should a re-fire wait for an in-flight run of the same partition to finish?
  2.  Performance. Does the DB have the right indices to support the new query patterns?
Thanks,
Jack

messages.subject: Re: [DISCUSS] Opt-in re-firing of asset partitions on late/corrected data
messages.body:
Hi Jack.

I think both points are valid. Yes, a re-fire max_active_runs will add
value in my opinion. We can't have multiple ones running. Furthermore, this
is for outside airflow (I think), the logic (Task) running should also take
race-condition into consideration to avoid collision and having a
max_active_run will mitigate to a point.

I think the DB (Postgres) will not be a bottleneck.

I have also made an initial PR for the suggested implementation, happy to
hear your feedback.

https://github.com/apache/airflow/pull/74583
